energy-ceasefire-collapse.title: Ukraine ends energy pause; Zelenskyy says 'we're done' with Trump ceasefire
energy-ceasefire-collapse.summary: President Zelenskyy told the Financial Times Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after a three-day pause requested by Washington. He said Russia struck Ukrainian energy infrastructure (Kyiv cited ~40 ballistic missiles in one assault) while Ukraine held fire. Russia said Ukraine hit a Ryazan-region refinery early Thursday. Zelenskyy also cited alleged limits on Starlink/Starshield mobility and reduced missile-warning intel; SpaceX's Musk said Starshield is US-government controlled. Trump's Sunday 'energy ceasefire' was tied to a US purchase of Russian diesel meant to ease US fuel prices before midterms.

analysis.text: Stated US goal was protecting energy infrastructure and cutting fuel prices; actual bargain mixed a diesel import deal with Moscow and pressure on Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refining. Collapse raises diesel/oil risk again and deepens Kyiv–Washington trust fracture ahead of Nov 3.

causes.why: Unilateral US energy ceasefire announcement failed when Russia kept striking Ukrainian energy and Kyiv ended its pause
US–Russia diesel deal was the political quid for pressing Kyiv to halt refinery strikes

houthis-saudi-oct15.title: Saudi coalition says cruise missile intercepted over Medina; Houthis keep targeting oil and airports
houthis-saudi-oct15.summary: On Oct 15 the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a cruise missile over the Medina region; Houthis called the claim a lie. On Oct 14 Houthis vowed more attacks on Saudi airports and oil after a strike that sources said heavily damaged Aramco's Dhahran HQ (Saudi Energy Ministry: limited fire). Riyadh King Khalid airport was hit Oct 10 (13 killed). Saudi-led strikes hit Sanaa-area fuel sites. Houthis swept to Bab el-Mandeb in September; Saudi-backed forces later pressed toward Mokha.

analysis.text: Stated Houthi motive is retaliation for Saudi strikes in Yemen; as Iran's proxy they open a second chokepoint (Bab el-Mandeb) while Hormuz burns, multiplying oil and Red Sea shipping risk without Tehran owning every shot.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct Houthi campaign against Saudi oil and airports
Same Iran-linked Gulf crisis: Hormuz pressure plus Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb second front

kabila-frn-succeeds-afc.title: Kabila's FRN dissolves AFC/M23 umbrella, claims Doha peace commitments
kabila-frn-succeeds-afc.summary: In a Goma statement dated Oct 14, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) led by ex-president Joseph Kabila said it had dissolved the Congo River Alliance (AFC) and assumed AFC's rights and Doha-process obligations. FRN was launched Oct 12 with M23 figures (incl. Sultani Makenga) as deputies. UN envoy Huang Xia told the Security Council a 'window of opportunity' remains via US- and Qatar-led tracks; illicit mineral trade still funds armed groups. M23 still holds Rubaya (~15% of world coltan).

analysis.text: Stated aim is national refoundation and honoring Doha; actual move consolidates Kabila's open leadership of the Rwanda-accused M23 mineral machine while keeping a diplomatic off-ramp. US–DRC minerals pact and AI/electronics demand make Rubaya leverage real.

causes.why: FRN is the formal successor structure to the Oct 12 Kabila–M23 coalition announcement

gfs-pride-sunk.title: Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sinks in Hormuz after projectile strike
gfs-pride-sunk.summary: The Singapore-registered container ship GFS Pride sank in the Strait of Hormuz after being struck by an unidentified projectile; all 21 crew were evacuated uninjured (Singapore MPA). UKMTO had reported the attack Tuesday; sister ship GFS Giselle was damaged. IRGC claimed a naval mine on an 'unauthorised' route; maritime firm Marisks said there is no independent evidence of mining. Reuters quoted Iranian officials saying Tehran is changing shipping tactics to keep oil prices high ahead of the Nov 3 US midterms. More than 20 vessels have been attacked this month in Hormuz, the Gulf and Gulf of Oman (UKMTO).

analysis.text: Stated motive is enforcing Iran's transit rules after the US blockade; real leverage is midterm oil-price pressure and forcing Washington to trade sanctions/blockade relief for shipping safety. Expanding beyond tankers to containers raises insurance and rerouting costs globally.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct surge in Iranian strikes on commercial shipping

pla-patrol-oct14-15.title: Taiwan tracks 15 PLA aircraft and 10 PLAN ships; median-line crossings continue
pla-patrol-oct14-15.summary: Taiwan's MND reported that from 06:00 Oct 14 to 06:00 Oct 15 it tracked 15 PLA aircraft, 10 PLAN ships and seven official ships; 13 aircraft crossed the median line into northern, central, southwestern and eastern ADIZ sectors. On Oct 14 alone it had reported 13 sorties with 11 median-line crossings during a 'joint combat readiness patrol.' China's announced live-fire window runs Oct 12–17.

analysis.text: Stated PLA framing is routine combat readiness; pressure after Lai's speech keeps Taiwan and US allies reacting while China retains rare-earth and chip-supply leverage into the Nov 10 control-suspension date.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct 12–17 live-fire / readiness patrol cycle after Lai's speech

energy-ceasefire.title: Russia spares Ukrainian energy for first time since Trump's 'energy ceasefire', pounds cities
energy-ceasefire.summary: Overnight into Oct 13, Russia struck cities and transport, killing at least four in Kharkiv, but hit no energy targets. On Oct 12 it had struck six energy sites. Neither side has confirmed the ceasefire, and the Kremlin rejected a 60-day truce.

analysis.text: The pause is fragile and unverifiable heading into winter.

causes.why: Energy-strike war began in October 2022

diesel-deal.title: US hopes Russian diesel deal can 'soften' Moscow on peace talks
diesel-deal.summary: Witkoff and Kushner told Ukrainian officials that a deal for Russia to supply more than 2.25M barrels of diesel could revive talks, and urged Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries. Zelensky called it a 'gift to Putin.'

analysis.text: High oil prices from the Gulf war give Russia energy leverage over US policy.

causes.why: Embargo rerouted Russian products and created today's leverage
Price-cap regime shapes Russian product sales

houthis-hit-aramco.title: Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports and oil after hitting Aramco HQ
houthis-hit-aramco.summary: On Oct 14 the Houthis vowed to keep striking Saudi airports and oil facilities, a day after a strike sources say badly damaged Aramco headquarters in Dhahran. An attack on Riyadh's King Khalid airport killed 13. The Houthis call this retaliation for Saudi backing of Yemeni government forces.

analysis.text: Iran gets a deniable second front against Gulf energy, while the Houthis pursue their own goal of holding the Red Sea coast and its revenue.

causes.why: Same Houthi playbook of striking Aramco to coerce Riyadh
De-escalation of 2022 never became a settlement

kabila-m23.title: Ex-DRC president Kabila launches coalition replacing M23-AFC
kabila-m23.summary: On Oct 13 Joseph Kabila launched a new political-military coalition to replace M23-AFC, which holds large areas of eastern DRC, including Goma.

analysis.text: Defections from the Congolese army and a collapse of the US/Qatar peace tracks are the main risks.

causes.why: M23's 2022 resurgence began today's war

hormuz-attacks-surge.title: Iran steps up Hormuz surveillance as tanker attacks soar and oil flows crash
hormuz-attacks-surge.summary: Iran deployed new units to watch the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler counted 10 tankers struck Sep 28–Oct 4; UKMTO counted 15 attacks Oct 6–14 (11 in the last four days). Flows fell from ~20.8M bbl on Oct 8 to 2.9M on Oct 11 (pre-war average 17.1M/day). The US keeps up its blockade of Iranian ports.

analysis.text: Iran is using control of the strait as bargaining leverage for sanctions relief, its frozen assets and an end to the blockade.

causes.why: OPEC+/Saudi oil leverage and US–Gulf friction persisted into the 2026 Gulf crisis

pla-drills.title: PLA live-fire drills in five sea areas after Lai speech; 11 aircraft cross median line
pla-drills.summary: China set drills Oct 12–17 in five sea areas while attacking President Lai's speech. Taiwan's MND reported 13 aircraft on Oct 14, 11 of which crossed the median line. China is also reportedly slowing germanium and quartz exports to Taiwan.

analysis.text: This is calibrated coercion rather than a sign of imminent action.

causes.why: 2022 drills set the template for encirclement exercises

pla-drills.unplaced: The drills were five sea areas, not one point.

kirovohrad-drone-barrage.title: Record Russian drone barrage hits Kirovohrad region during 'energy truce'
kirovohrad-drone-barrage.summary: Kirovohrad region suffered its largest Russian attack of the war overnight: 360+ drones hit 26 locations, killing three and wounding six (Gov. Andriy Raikovych). Ukraine's air force said 580 drones were launched nationwide, 536 shot down.

analysis.text: Strikes of this scale on infrastructure are the stated reason Kyiv abandoned the energy pause; expect tit-for-tat refinery and grid strikes to resume at pace.

kirovohrad-drone-barrage.unplaced: Governor reported 26 locations across Kirovohrad region; no single site named.

houthis-hit-aden-palace.title: Houthi missiles hit Aden presidential palace, killing five
houthis-hit-aden-palace.summary: Houthis fired missiles and drones at Aden's Al-Maashiq presidential palace complex, seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, killing five and wounding 16 (Yemeni health minister). The PM and cabinet were safe. It is the first strike on the palace in the current Houthi-Saudi conflict. The coalition said Houthis made 20 attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid airport this month (17 killed, 333 wounded); ICAO's council condemned attacks on Saudi civil aviation.

causes.why: Escalation of the Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies

analysis.text: Hitting the government seat signals the Houthis will widen the war beyond Saudi territory to the Yemeni government itself, raising pressure on the Mokha/Bab el-Mandeb front and on Riyadh to escalate or negotiate.
